html:
SMTO-POL-0006 — SMTO can't override the job that is blocking your task

GUID: bee95df2-7fc4-4c09-b6c9-50895322e612
Slug: resource-override-not-eligible
Domain: POL · Subsystem: pol

What happened

  • Your task is waiting because an earlier job may still be using the same thing it needs. SMTO refused to push ahead anyway, because this situation doesn't qualify for that. Your command has not started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page and open the conversation so the task's recovery card shows its current state. The card only offers the choices SMTO will accept right now, and an override is not one of them.
  2. Select Wait until the job state changes on the task's recovery card if the earlier job might still be working. SMTO continues by itself once that job is done. Waiting lets the earlier job finish first, so the two never change the same thing at once.
  3. Select Resolve forcefully by terminating job only if you are sure the earlier job is no longer needed. The button is greyed out when SMTO can't stop it safely. Stopping the earlier job frees what your task needs without two jobs working on it together.

What success looks like

  • The recovery card shows 'Job state updated.' or 'Blocking job claims restored.', and the task then continues.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with a note about what the earlier job was doing, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep repeating the override request; it will be refused the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway rejected a resource override because the recovery candidate ID, the source operation's recorded resource scope, or the blockers' state (all must have liveness_state=unknown and resource_claim_state=reconciliation_required) did not meet the override rules.

What this means

  • Resource override requires a recognized recovery operation, a retained resource scope and blockers with unknown liveness and reconciliation-required claims. Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Resource override requires a recognized recovery operation, a retained resource scope and blockers with unknown liveness and reconciliation-required claims.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the candidate recovery identity, resource scope, blocker liveness and claim state; a known live owner needs a different recovery action.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the run's external_resource_reconciliation prerequisite and its blockers (GatewayJobs._commit_blocker_control in gateway_core/jobs.py). Use the wait or reset action the recovery projection currently enables; override is kept only for persisted decisions and older clients and requires an op_recovery candidate, a recorded resource_scope and every blocker in liveness_state=unknown with resource_claim_state=reconciliation_required.
  • Inspect the blocker and use an offered recovery action; do not bypass ownership or evidence checks.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected supported recovery action matches the current blocker evidence and its eligibility rules.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
